utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please call the case, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Now, this Thursday I greet -- I welcome everybody, representatives of the Prosecution and the Defence, as well as the accused and all the people who are helping us in our work. We will now continue the examination of the witness, and I will therefore ask now the registrar to lower the blinds unless there is some question. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. Before proceedings this morning, we handed over for the Trial Chamber and for the Prosecutor parts of the transcript or, rather, the statement this witness made to the investigators that we used, and they have been separated with pieces of paper and a pink marker indicates the excerpt that we used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we are going into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please lift the blinds. As far as next week is concerned - I shall not give the name of the witness - the Prosecution will have five hours, undoubtedly much less. Let's assume that we use that as a working basis. The Defence will have the same. And if you cannot agree amongst yourselves, Mr. Coric will have an hour and a half; Mr. Stojic will have an hour and 15 minutes; Mr. Prlic will have one hour; Mr. Praljak will have 45 minutes; Mr. Petkovic will have 45 minutes; Mr. Pusic, 45 minutes. Six hours all in all for the Defence counsel. Also, second announcement I'd like to make, I shall read this out slowly. Pursuant to Rule 67(A) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, the Trial Chamber -- the Trial Chamber would have to set a deadline for the Defence so that it can inform the Prosecution whether or not it wishes to invoke a defence of alibi or a special -- or any special defence. Before setting such a deadline, the Trial Chamber would like to know what the opinion of both parties is. In other words, according to them, at what point in time should the Defence inform the Prosecutor of such an intention. The Trial Chamber would like to get the position of both parties on this matter in writing by Wednesday, the 19th of September, 2007, at the latest. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I apologise to you, Mr. Karnavas, for interrupting you, but it is still a kind of correction here. When the President has announced about the partition of the time, then he said that the Prosecution will have five hours, and then he added later on, but probably it was the wrong translation, that the Defence will have the same, that is, five hours. But later on when he detailed the partition for the Defence, then he said that altogether six hours. So I would only like to clarify that the Prosecution will have five hours and the Defence six hours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I did say. Five hours for the Prosecution, is six hours for the Defence. Maybe there was a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President; good morning, Your Honours. My concerns are with respect to a witness coming up, Mr. Miller. We have yet to receive the decision. We know that we should be getting it by the end of the week. My concerns are that the Prosecution has added on their exhibit list certain presidential transcripts. Now, in keeping with the previous ruling with respect to an OTP employee, Mr. Sudetic, this Trial Chamber found that it did not need Mr. Sudetic to come in and read or interpret the transcription for you. Mr. Miller is in the same position. Initially his report dealt with reading newspaper clippings and basically telling us what was former US President Ulysses Grant said, "War is hell." I think that's the essence of his testimony. We don't need an expert to tell us that during war bad things happen. But I am concerned that now they're trying to sneak in through the basement window where they can't come in the front door. The front door has been bolted. They were told Sudetic cannot come and now they want to use Miller because maybe his pedigree, he's got a Ph.D. as I understand it, maybe because of that, they think Mr. Miller can come in and opine about certain events with respect to what was being said and recorded in these presidential transcripts. So therefore, Your Honour, I would ask that we get some clarification on this. I am of the belief and I've stated this that Mr. Miller is not an expert and offers nothing, zero. His report is not even a report, it's laughable if -- if you could laugh at it. And I don't think that we should be wasting time with this sort of testimony and I suggest that we get an early ruling so that the Prosecution can make further arrangements to fill in that week with some witnesses as opposed to coming back saying, "Well, we didn't have enough time to bring in another witness." So we lose that one week of time. So that's my concern, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Stringer, just something which probably escaped me, but Mr. Miller, like Mr. Sudetic, is employed by the OTP; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I don't think so, Mr. President. I don't think he's an employee of the OTP. And on this -- and on this point I've got to confess that I don't have a lot of information that I can provide the Trial Chamber with respect to this witness. The one thing I can say for sure is that if Mr. Miller is not permitted to testify next week then we will have another week of no evidence, because today being Thursday and again we'll have the situation that we had recently. So I don't know that we could recover at this late date if Miller does not testify. Beyond that, what's happening in respect to the transcripts or whether -- further information about his status regretfully, Mr. President, I can't inform you. I can -- I can get informed if I can reach the people and provide more information to you, but at this moment I can't do it and I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps you misunderstood me. Sudetic was the in-house Prosecution employee, and so since they can't use him now they've gone to outside experts who prepared another report, but that has nothing to do really with the presidential transcripts. And my concern is why is it that we need to have an expert to talk -- to read and opine on the transcripts when you can do that yourselves, and that was the ruling on Sudetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer, just one point of clarification. Next week, a witness has been scheduled for four days, so that will not be a problem because Mr. Miller had been scheduled for the week after that, and the Trial Chamber deliberated on the matter yesterday. We're going to hand down a decision on this in the next few hours. I was going say in a split second; that's not the case. In the next few hours. So given that the deadline is 4.00 in the afternoon. So the decision will be made before 4.00 this afternoon. If there are no further questions, I'd like to thank all the people in this courtroom, and we shall meet again on Monday at a quarter past 2.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 17th day of September, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.50 a.m.,
